history.title: טולי והים שבא והולך
history.summary: Tuli, a small sea turtle on the Tel Aviv beach, notices the sea coming and going. Grandma turtle explains that the Moon's gentle pull makes the tides; here the sea moves only a turtle's step, in far places it climbs a giant staircase. Refrain: ששש... הים בא. ששש... הים הולך. Music: Debussy, Clair de lune.

history.title: Mira and the Magnet That Loved Metal
history.summary: Mira, four, is given a little red horseshoe magnet from her grandfather's toolbox. It grabs the spoon and the nail but ignores wood, paper, plastic and glass, and she is afraid it is broken; sorting a click pile and a quiet pile she finds the real rule. The true fact: a magnet only pulls things with iron inside (iron, steel, nickel, cobalt), which is why the aluminium can and the copper coin stay put even though they are metal. Refrain: Click! The magnet grabs. Shhh. The magnet lets go. No music.

history.title: הלב הקטן של תום
history.summary: Tom, four, jumps and dances with Muki the cat before bed, then lies down, feels a fast bum-bum in his chest and is frightened by it. His mother explains that the heart is a muscle about the size of his own fist which sends blood everywhere in the body; it works faster when the muscles ask for more air, and it calms down when he breathes slowly with her. The true fact: heart rate rises with effort and falls at rest, a child's heart beats faster than a grown-up's (and a cat's faster still), and the heart keeps working even during sleep. Refrain: בום־בום. בום־בום. הלב של תום אומר שלום. Music: Brahms, Wiegenlied (Lullaby), sung by Renée Fleming.

music.title: Brahms – Wiegenlied (Lullaby), op. 49 no. 4 (Renée Fleming, Hartmut Höll)

history.title: Sol the Snail and the Silver Trail
history.summary: Sol, a small garden snail, wants to reach the flat board on top of the garden fence to see the first star of the night, but the wood goes straight up and she slides back down and gives up. Nana Snail, old and mossy-shelled, tells her to look behind her at her own long silver trail: her slime holds her like glue when she is still and turns slippery when she pushes, so she practises on a stone and then climbs the post, bit by bit, until she reaches the top and the star. The true fact: a snail's pedal mucus is viscoelastic, gripping like a solid adhesive at rest and flowing like a lubricant under the shear of the foot's muscle waves, which is how snails hold on to vertical walls and still glide forward; most snails move less than about 8 cm a minute. Refrain: Slide and stick. Slide and stick. Little by little, bit by bit. No music.

options.title: טליה והגלגל שמרים
options.summary: Talia wants to help lift a heavy bucket of water for Grandpa and discovers that winding a rope around a wheel — a pulley — makes the heavy work feel light.

options.title: הפינה השקטה של נועה
options.summary: Noa feels alone at a noisy playground until she finds a quiet corner where a shy new friend is drawing, and together they learn that saying a feeling out loud can make it smaller.

options.title: דני סופר כוכבים
options.summary: Before sleep, Dani counts the stars appearing one by one over the roof and notices they blink in a repeating pattern, bright-soft-bright-soft, and grandma calls it a pattern.

options.title: האורות הרוקדים בארץ הקרח
options.summary: Little Sanna in the far north can't fall asleep until she watches soft green and purple lights ripple silently across the night sky, and Grandmother explains they are the aurora — sunlight's tiny particles glowing high above the snow.
options.music: Jean Sibelius – Valse triste (soft strings, evokes the quiet shimmering lights)

options.title: תום הקטן שרצה לבקוע ביצים
options.summary: As a curious boy, young Thomas Edison sits for hours on a nest of goose eggs to see if he can hatch them himself, and learns that eggs need a steady, gentle warmth to become chicks.
